example_sentences.japanese: 世界で一番高い山はどこですか。
example_sentences.english: Where is the tallest mountain in the world?

example_sentences.japanese: 祖父は船で世界を旅行しました。
example_sentences.english: My grandfather traveled around the world by ship.

example_sentences.japanese: 娘は地図を見ながら、世界の海の名前を覚えています。
example_sentences.english: My daughter is memorizing the names of the world's oceans while looking at a map.

example_sentences.japanese: 叔父は政治の話が好きなので、晩ご飯が長くなります。
example_sentences.english: My uncle loves talking politics, so dinner always runs long.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は政治のことがあまり分かりません。
example_sentences.english: I don't really understand much about politics.

example_sentences.japanese: 大学で政治を勉強したいと思っています。
example_sentences.english: I'm thinking I'd like to study politics at university.

example_sentences.japanese: 会議で自分の意見を言うのは難しいです。
example_sentences.english: It's hard to give your own opinion in a meeting.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生はみんなの意見を聞いてから、答えを教えてくれました。
example_sentences.english: The teacher heard everyone's opinions first, then told us the answer.

example_sentences.japanese: 姉に電話して、意見を聞きました。
example_sentences.english: I called my older sister and asked for her opinion.

example_sentences.japanese: 外国人の友達に日本の文化を紹介しました。
example_sentences.english: I introduced Japanese culture to a friend from abroad.

example_sentences.japanese: 外国の文化を知るために、よく映画を見ます。
example_sentences.english: I often watch movies to learn about other cultures.

example_sentences.japanese: この町には古い文化が残っています。
example_sentences.english: This town still keeps its old culture.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎年、祖母と伝統の料理を作ります。
example_sentences.english: Every year I make traditional dishes with my grandmother.

example_sentences.japanese: この店には百年の伝統があります。
example_sentences.english: This shop has a hundred years of tradition.

example_sentences.japanese: 若い人は、あまり伝統の服を着なくなりました。
example_sentences.english: Young people don't wear traditional clothes much anymore.

example_sentences.japanese: 息子は春から社会に出ます。
example_sentences.english: My son goes out into the working world this spring.

example_sentences.japanese: 社会はだんだん便利になりました。
example_sentences.english: Society has gradually become more convenient.

example_sentences.japanese: 社会のために働く人になりたいです。
example_sentences.english: I want to become someone who works for the good of society.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は国際会議で英語を話しました。
example_sentences.english: She spoke English at an international conference.

example_sentences.japanese: 兄は国際問題の本をたくさん読んでいます。
example_sentences.english: My older brother reads lots of books on international issues.

example_sentences.japanese: 国際社会の中で、日本は何ができるでしょうか。
example_sentences.english: What can Japan do within the international community?

example_sentences.japanese: 政府は町に新しい病院を作ります。
example_sentences.english: The government is going to build a new hospital in the town.

example_sentences.japanese: 叔母は政府の仕事をしています。
example_sentences.english: My aunt works for the government.

example_sentences.japanese: 政府の意見に反対する人も多いです。
example_sentences.english: Plenty of people disagree with the government's view.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供にも遊ぶ権利があります。
example_sentences.english: Children have the right to play, too.

example_sentences.japanese: 働く人には休む権利があります。
example_sentences.english: Working people have the right to rest.

example_sentences.japanese: お金を払ったので、私たちにはこの席に座る権利があります。
example_sentences.english: We paid, so we have every right to sit in these seats.

example_sentences.japanese: 法律で、ここに車を止めてはいけません。
example_sentences.english: By law, you can't park your car here.

example_sentences.japanese: 法律の本は、言葉がとても難しいです。
example_sentences.english: The words in law books are really difficult.

example_sentences.japanese: 来月から法律が変わるので、会社は準備しています。
example_sentences.english: The law changes next month, so the company is getting ready.
